newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro-stocks fall ahead of US inflation data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro-stocks fall ahead of US inflation data.

text.p: European stocks fell in nervous trading on Tuesday with investors keeping a wary eye open for U.S. inflation figures due later in the day for pointers on the direction of interest rates.
In foreign exchanges, the dollar gained on the mark, which was still hurt by worries over a soft single European currency, and strengthened slightly against the yen.

London, which set a cracking pace last week with three closing peaks, lost early gains to show losses of 0.9 percent as investors fretted about possible bad news in the country's budget next month. Wall Street, which ended down overnight after smashing six records last week, provided no encouragement .
The FTSE 100 index of leading shares was down steeply by lunchtime in trade that was said to be quiet ahead of major horse-race and cricket fixtures in the sporting calendar next week.
"I think the market is waiting to see what will happen in the budget and with Ascot and the Test match (cricket) this week. I can see it getting quieter and quieter," said one sales trader.
The London market was expected to remain edgy after reports on Monday that the government could cut valuable tax breaks for pension funds in the July 2 budget.

"We are going to have Budget blues," another trader said. "There's just no reason to buy this market." Another factor clouding sentiment was the May U.S. inflation data, due at 1230 GMT, and its implications for U.S. interest rates.

"We're only three weeks away from the budget now and I think the market will continue to be nervous," said one trader. "We still look vulnerable to more profit-taking because there's a lot of profits to be taken."
British government bonds were steady as the market absorbed the implications of the Amsterdam EU summit's approval of the budget stability pact and a resolution on boosting employment and growth.
In Frankfurt, floor trade was down sharplly , at 0.7 percent, by midday with Monday's drop on Wall Street removing the impetus for some of the recent gains.
"There is a lot of nervousness around and a lot of it is related to the negotiations at the Amsterdam summit," said one trader of the European Union summit.

Paris, which saw volatile trading on Monday after touching a trading peak, slipped by 0.7 percent amid nerves over the data on U.S. consumer prices for May in thin trade. "it's very calm," a trader said.
In currencies, the dollar climbed by nearly a pfennig to
1.7363 marks with the German currency under pressure and the dollar benefiting from its safe haven reputation as the stability pact improved prospects for a weak single currency.

"Overall people do think EMU will progress and that the chances are it will be a weak one -- that's a reason the dollar's fairly well underpinned," said Alan Collins, head of technical analysis at Merita Bank in London.

Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp's comment that EMU delay made no sense helped keep the mark subdued. Talk of delay usually boosts the mark as fears recede that it will be replaced by a flimsier single currency.

The U.S. currency strengthened slightly against the yen despite traders focusing attention on this week's Japanese May trade data, expected to show a growing surplus, and U.S. April figures, where a worsening deficit, is expected..

Anticipation of the data has added spice to speculation ahead of the Group of Seven industrial nations meeting in Denver on June 20-22. The market fears that the expanding trade gap will see sparks fly between the U.S. and Japan. A stronger dollar helps Japanese exports.
Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered, said the U.S. was concerned about trade but not to the point that they were willing to engage heavily in exchange rate rhetoric.
"The issue is to try to get Japan to boost demand and how they do that, rather than by trying to engineer a manipulation of exchange rates," said Fox.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7365 marks and 113.75 yen, compared with 1.7291 and 113.39 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 40.6 points at 4704.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 13.79 points at 2782.08.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 23.63 points at 3741.48.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $341.40 an ounce, compared with Monday's close of $341.75. Silver was unchanged at $4.72.
